_comment: Finding N (audit): demo-data/products.csv has no surcharge_rule/early_discount_rule/rounding_rule columns at all — the generator baked already-computed figures straight into assessments.csv instead of expressing a reusable rule. This file is genuine project configuration (not demo-data, not TypeScript source) applied once by scripts/seed.ts's applyProductDerivedRules() after products load. A new product's rule is an edit to this file, never a code change. Only PSCA-CHALLAN-MOV is seeded: it's the one product in the whole 164-assessment pack with a real, fully-isolable, nonzero discount_applied_minor (AS-00072, PSID 41011300000190123 — exactly 25% of principal, discount_expires_on = issue_date + 10 days = 2026-08-01), and these exact parameter values (25%, 10 days) are §15.4's own worked-example numbers, not invented here. No surcharge_rule is seeded for any product — see the per-entry note below.

rules._note: Verified against demo-data/assessments.csv AS-00072: assessed_amount_minor=500000, discount_applied_minor=125000 (exactly 25%), issue_date=2026-07-22, and the resulting discount_expires_on=2026-08-01 matches spec/openapi.yaml's own illustrative example for this same field.

_surcharge_note: No surcharge_rule is seeded for any product. The two LEA-17-1000 anchor payables that are OVERDUE (AS-00057, AS-00073) both show surcharge_accrued_minor=0 in demo-data despite being overdue — while 10 OTHER ETPB-TOKEN-CAR assessments elsewhere in the pack carry a nonzero baked-in surcharge. This means the generator's real surcharge logic is more nuanced than a uniform DAILY_SIMPLE-from-due-date rule, and reverse-engineering it exactly isn't achievable from documented, non-invented configuration. computeDerived's surcharge mechanism (§15.4, DAILY_SIMPLE/ACT_365/capped) is real and unit-tested directly — it's just not switched on for any product via this file, which is an honest, reported gap rather than a guess.
